problem: Find the point of intersection of the parabola ${y}^{2}-x+10y+21=0$ with the $x$-axis.

feedback.problem: Find the points of intersection of the parabola ${x}^{2}=\frac{3}{7}(y+4)$ with the $x$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we set $y=0$ and solve the resulting equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =\frac{3}{7}(0+4) \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{12}{7} \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{12}{7}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the intersection points are
 $(\sqrt{\frac{12}{7}},0)$ and $(-\sqrt{\frac{12}{7}},0).$
